counterfactual_missing_items: No chronic crypt architectural distortion or granulomas to support inflammatory bowel disease
No history of allogeneic stem cell transplantation to support graft-versus-host disease
No chemotherapy-associated apoptotic crypt injury pattern to support chemotherapy-induced colitis
decisive_items: The histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains.

marked expansion of the lamina propria by a dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate predominantly composed of pale histiocytes with vacuolated cytoplasm admixed with eosinophils, neutrophils, and lymphocytes
multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
response.rationale: C1 best integrates the pathognomonic von Kossa/PAS-positive targetoid basophilic inclusions (Michaelis-Gutmann bodies) in pale histiocytes with the rectosigmoid polyp distribution, giving the most complete diagnosis of GI malakoplakia. R3 is the same entity but less anatomically complete and is discounted as a correlated restatement. R1 is the closest clinical alternative but cannot explain the inclusion-bearing histiocytic infiltrate; R2 and R4 are not supported by the histology.

rejected.why: No allogeneic transplant history; GVHD histology would show epithelial apoptosis/crypt dropout, not von Kossa/PAS-positive histiocytic inclusions.
Same core diagnosis as C1 but lacks anatomic specificity; discounted as correlated restatement.
Chemotherapy is a nonspecific contextual risk factor and does not explain the pathognomonic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies in histiocytes.
